events.title: Netscape Navigator 2.0 shipped
events.summary: Netscape released Navigator 2.0 on March 18, 1996 — the first mass-market browser with JavaScript and support for Java applets and plug-ins.
events.about: Navigator 2.0 made pages programmable: form validation, image rollovers, and early dynamic UI without reloading. It also embraced third-party plug-ins (QuickTime, Acrobat) and frames — for better or worse, shaping how 1990s sites were built.

narrative.whyChosen: This was the first browser millions used that could run JavaScript in the wild.
narrative.whyImportant: It turned the browser from a document viewer into an application runtime.
narrative.problemSolved: Static HTML could not deliver interactive pages; Netscape needed to ship the scripting language it had invented.

events.title: Palm Pilot 1000 released
events.summary: U.S. Robotics' Palm Computing division began selling the Palm Pilot 1000 in March 1996 — a pocket PDA with Graffiti handwriting and HotSync desktop software.
events.about: The Pilot fit in a shirt pocket and synced contacts and calendars to a PC with one button press. Developers wrote Palm OS apps in C; the platform dominated PDAs until smartphones absorbed its use cases. Graffiti input and the app launcher UI influenced early mobile design before touchscreens took over.

narrative.whyChosen: The Palm Pilot made PDAs mainstream and created a thriving third-party app ecosystem.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved millions would carry a dedicated pocket computer for personal information management.
narrative.problemSolved: Paper planners and bulky laptops could not keep mobile professionals organized on the go.
